limitations_and_boundaries: Less than 20% of drug-dose combinations in sci-Plex3 deviate from controls by more than 35% in r2, indicating technical noise.
Drugs from only a few pathways (tyrosine kinase signaling, DNA damage and repair, cell cycle regulation, epigenetic regulation) show clear effects.

research_questions.statement: Can we predict single-cell transcriptional responses to unseen drug perturbations by combining a compositional perturbation autoencoder with molecular structure encoding and transfer learning from bulk RNA HTS?

claims.statement: Pretraining on bulk RNA HTS (L1000) improves chemCPA's generalization performance to unseen drugs, even when the single-cell gene set differs from the bulk set.

claims.statement: chemCPA outperforms CPA and scGen on the task of predicting unseen drug-covariate combinations.

claims.statement: chemCPA can generalize to unseen drugs, a task that cannot be modeled using CPA or scGen.

methods.name: chemCPA
methods.protocol_description: Chemical compositional perturbation autoencoder: an encoder-decoder architecture that encodes molecular structures of drugs (via a molecule encoder G) into latent perturbations, uses a non-linear dosage scaler S, and disentangles basal state from perturbation attributes via adversarial training (gradient reversal). Transfer learning is performed by pretraining on L1000 bulk RNA data and fine-tuning on sci-Plex3 single-cell data, handling differing gene sets via a projection layer or shared gene subset.
